security_spec.violation_condition: The kernel reads shpmsdetailsbt1 or shpmsdetailsbt2 when a sample was taken during kernel-mode execution, and exposes the raw branch target PCs to userspace via the perf sample record without zeroing or applying KASLR offset masking. Additionally, if the kernel does not context-switch (save/restore) these CSRs on thread migration, branch targets from one address space leak into another.
security_spec.summary: New Sspesa shpmsdetailsbt1/2 CSRs capture branch target PCs that, when sampled in kernel context, carry raw kernel code addresses; exposing these in userspace perf sample records bypasses KASLR unless the kernel explicitly sanitizes the record before delivery.

findings.finding: The RISC-V PMU driver explicitly rejects PERF_SAMPLE_BRANCH_STACK requests with -EOPNOTSUPP at event_init time. This means perf branch stack sampling — the only path through which shpmsdetailsbt1/2 CSR values could reach userspace — is completely blocked at the entry point. No branch target PC leak is possible.

No CSR definitions exist for shpmsdetailsbt1, shpmsdetailsbt2, or any other Sspesa CSRs. The kernel has zero awareness of the Sspesa ISA extension, so no code path exists that could read and expose these branch target PC registers.
findings.snippet: (No shpmsdetailsbt1/2 or Sspesa-related CSR definitions present in csr.h)

findings.finding: The core perf output path’s PERF_SAMPLE_BRANCH_STACK handling (lines 8262-8288) copies struct perf_branch_entry records to userspace. This is a generic mechanism; each architecture's PMU driver is responsible for populating data->br_stack. Since the RISC-V PMU driver never populates br_stack and rejects branch sampling at init, the generic code path is never reached from a RISC-V context. No RISC-V-specific masking or zeroing is needed because no data flows here.
The RISC-V perf callchain implementation walks kernel stack frames via walk_stackframe(). It does not interact with branch target CSRs or any Sspesa registers. No information leak through this path.
